62:

64:

66: - `runtime_paths`: reproducible but performance- or capability-critical runtime equipment, such as Hermes-managed uv, Tirith, and its LSP layer;

102: ## Network continuity boundary
103: 
104: Workstation owns physical route selection and exposes it as explicit transport capabilities rather than asking each Agent or domain to understand interfaces, VPNs, or policy-table numbers. The current `ambient` profile follows the machine's ordinary route and deliberately makes no global-reachability guarantee. `native-a` and `native-b` are HTTPS CONNECT sidecars bound to loopback; each sidecar runs under a dedicated policy-routing identity, opens only public IPv4 TCP/443 destinations, never terminates TLS, and therefore lets the caller retain its own filesystem and credential authority while the outbound socket follows a VPN-independent native path. `netprofile show <profile>` returns a deterministic `profileDigest` covering the transport profile and referenced route profile. Effectful execution is fail-closed: `netprofile run --expect <profileDigest> <profile> -- <absolute executable> ...` refuses stale bindings, projects the selected HTTPS transport through standard proxy environment variables, and exports both profile name and digest to the child. Applications that do not honor HTTPS proxy variables are not covered by this profile.
105: 
106: Cloudflare control-plane ingress consumes the same native route substrate. `ordivon-cloudflare-production-a.service`, `ordivon-cloudflare-production-b.service`, and `ordivon-cloudflare-canary.service` run under the two native routing identities, while a local DoH stub at `127.0.0.55` keeps edge discovery independent of VPN DNS. When two native defaults are present, A and B select different physical paths even if WSL mirrors them onto the same IPv4 prefix and gateway. When only one native path exists, both profiles deliberately converge on it and the doctor reports reduced physical-path diversity as a warning. Destination reachability remains a measured capability: one native path can reach Cloudflare and DeepSeek while still failing GitHub. `netprofile matrix` labels its output `truthRole=point-in-time-observation` and timestamps both the matrix window and each target probe; an old matrix is evidence of what was observed, never durable current network truth. World consumes a selected transport and does not become a network router; Runtime remains the owner of local execution and need not add network routing to `ExecutionProfile`.
107: 
108: `netcontinuity` closes a failure mode that route structure cannot detect. A VPN may leave its adapter, services and capture routes present while its real data plane is dead; in that state tables 201/202 can remain structurally correct while Windows WFP still blocks both native egress identities. The continuity observer therefore combines Surfshark capture state with bounded destination probes through `ambient`, `native-a` and `native-b`, and writes a point-in-time observation under `/root/.local/state/ordivon-workstation/network-continuity`. The observer never mutates VPN state. `failover-direct --expect <observationDigest>` is a separate effect: it only accepts a fresh `vpn_capture_half_dead` observation, re-observes the fault, requires an Administrator Windows token, releases Surfshark's capture, reconciles the native route tables and proves at least one direct destination capability. `restore-vpn --expect <failoverReceiptDigest>` starts Surfshark and invokes its own UI `connect_button`, then requires both capture routes and ambient destination service before claiming restoration. 109: 
110: `surfpath` adds a separate Workstation-owned egress capability without promoting Surfshark into network authority. Secret authority remains outside the repository: manual WireGuard configs live under the Surfshark secret root, while imported OpenVPN TCP/UDP configs plus the two-line `auth-user-pass` authority live under the OpenVPN secret root. `surfpath catalog` projects only safe transport metadata and config digests. WireGuard execution is pinned to an exact upstream `wireguard-go` revision and receipted binary digest; OpenVPN execution is bound to the exact Workstation package version and `/usr/bin/openvpn` digest. The provider catalog therefore distinguishes `wireguard`, `openvpn-tcp` and `openvpn-udp` as separate transport variants rather than treating one Surfshark location as one path.
111: 
112: `surfpath discover --write` probes bounded tuples of native ingress, protocol, logical Surfshark node and currently resolved endpoint IP inside transient network namespaces. WireGuard qualification requires a real handshake; OpenVPN qualification requires `Initialization Sequence Completed`. The Linux OpenVPN runtime overlay pins the observed endpoint IP, references the external credential authority, explicitly declares `dev-type tun`, admits the provider's legacy CBC fallback during cipher negotiation, and ignores Surfshark's Windows-only `block-outside-dns` push without modifying the source `.ovpn` authority. Qualified paths are ranked, but ranking is advisory; the observation records `recommendedPathDigest` and `rankedPaths` rather than silently granting execution authority to rank 1.
113: 
114: Effectful use is scoped and Agent-selected. `surfpath run --expect <observationDigest> --path <pathDigest> -- <absolute executable> ...` accepts only a fresh schema-v2 observation and only a path digest that was qualified in that exact observation. It revalidates the current ingress, transport config digest, exact provider binary identity and exact Surfshark endpoint binding, reconstructs the selected WireGuard/OpenVPN tunnel, and re-probes required destinations before running the child. Frozen destination addresses from discovery are tried first, while current path-local Surfshark DNS answers may be used as fallback because CDN addresses are reality rather than durable authority. In every protocol, a successful tunnel is still insufficient: actual Cloudflare egress plus required destination service are separately observed. Frozen destination addresses from discovery are tried first, while current path-local Surfshark DNS answers may be used as fallback because CDN addresses are reality rather than durable authority.
